# Private Markets authenticated transport qualification

This branch adds an isolated Request/Response handler, explicitly configured HTTPS transport and disposable view-scoped client over the frozen private retained SQL reader. SQL, roles, grants and public endpoint actions are unchanged. There is no deployed entrypoint or default endpoint.

The handler requires a server-configured exact HTTPS-origin allowlist, source namespace, verified bearer-authentication function and parameterized query function. Browser JSON contains only investigation/workspace/asset/event IDs and an explicit-offset microsecond timestamp. Cookies and caller identity/rights/reviewer/observation authority flags are rejected. Authentication must be verified server-side; JWT decoding/user-editable metadata is not an acceptable implementation. No provider authentication is configured by this package.

Requests are limited to4096bytes, responses to1048576bytes; streams and operations have deadlines/abort handling. No cookies, cache, redirects, token persistence or automatic retries. Client disposal/new requests suppress late successes and denials even if an injected adapter ignores AbortSignal. Expected observation ID is supplied from the already-loaded workspace context for result matching, never sent as database authority.

The strict private mapper rejects unknown keys, promoted publication/lineage/history flags, mismatched scope/observation/time, malformed endpoint-version adjacency and Unicode span lengths. It retains issuer/network and shared-node versions, aliases, actual excerpt material hashes/spans and nullable source metadata. Unsafe/non-HTTP(S)/userinfo URLs are suppressed rather than made actionable. Date-only published/identity metadata stays text; no midnight event time, rights-cleared state, provenance or independent root is invented. Response instant equivalence uses the existing marketInstant parser with at most microsecond precision; request timestamp spelling is retained for display.

Meaningful sanitized outcomes distinguish401authentication,403access/origin denial,400malformed requests,409evidence unavailable or resource saturation, and503transient/invalid backend responses. No raw SQL/Auth diagnostics or private payload is logged.

Native qualification invokes actual Request -> handler -> createPrivateMarketsReader -> PostgreSQL PREPARE/EXECUTE as mip_hypothesis_gateway, then the strict client mapper. Authentication is an explicit synthetic bearer-to-fixture-user mapping; rights grants remain the existing synthetic admin-created native fixture. This is not real provider verification, browser networking/CORS enforcement, deployment, publication, or real-source authority qualification. Unknown production readers, source-root lineage, full attribution/rights, zero-path asset card, larger corpus scale and complete Markets UI remain blocked/incomplete as documented by the base package.

name: Hypothesis durable worker isolation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'supabase/qualification/hypothesis-assessments/**'
      - 'supabase/qualification/mip-cutover-authority/**'
      - 'supabase/functions/source-comparison-generation-candidate/**'
      - 'src/lib/hypothesisAssessment*.js'

permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  worker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17.6
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: mip-disposable-ci-only
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres"
          --health-interval 5s

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.0.0

      - name: Install locked verifier dependencies without package scripts
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit

      - name: Enable metadata decoding in the existing disposable service
        env:
          MIP_DISPOSABLE_POSTGRES: comparison-qualification
          MIP_POSTGRES_SERVICE_ID: ${{ job.services.postgres.id }}
        run: node verifier/hypothesis-worker/prepareLogical.mjs
      - name: Synthetic native authority and actual worker restart tests
        env:
          MIP_DISPOSABLE_POSTGRES: comparison-qualification

        run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 verifier/hypothesis-worker/*.test.mjs

# Private retained Markets qualification — work in progress

This opt-in package extends shared public.nodes/public.edges identities and evidence_pipeline history/candidates in a disposable native fixture. It does not deploy a Markets tab, publish graph records, enable quote providers, ingest real material, or complete Markets.

Typed equity, cryptoasset and network nodes remain separate canonical identities. Exact issuer/network companion versions, endpoint node versions and shared edge versions are retained in the same evidence history. The new typed_graph_relationship candidate branch preserves existing event-only candidates. Assessment context adds all exact endpoint/edge/companion change positions to the existing dependency machinery.

The private reader checks current workspace membership, exact retained observation membership and six operation scopes per material (rights/privacy × retention/analysis/excerpt_display). It holds the existing publication/revocation fence through the read, uses sorted material identities, verifies stored Unicode spans through the existing retained_excerpt function, and returns only bounded private projections. The trusted server seam injects the authenticated user and configured source; client inputs contain identities and valid time only.

Private shared graph records require a protected suppression discriminator. Restrictive policies exclude them even when old permissive raw policies exist. Public edges cannot expose private endpoints. The known definer aggregate explicitly excludes private nodes/edges and private endpoint citations. Installation refuses additional catalog-discoverable exposed dependent views; dynamic SQL/functions and the full production surface inventory still require review. This is not a general publication eligibility flag and there is no private-to-public promotion function.

Fixture parity is limited: existing hypothesis fixtures supply actual native evidence/workspace/permission functions, strengthened with the observed seven-type node check and endpoint UUID foreign-key/non-self-edge constraints. The actual survivor currently lacks the old historical edges_type_check; the fixture does not pretend otherwise. Public/source schema, owners, grants and all live readers have not been fully mirrored. Production installation remains BLOCKED.

The SQL and fixture presently qualify bounded typed path mechanics in both directions, with synthetic equity/crypto and indirect relationships. Recorded supported assessments are not independent validation of real-world claims or method calibration. All source passages, identities, authority receipts and relationships in tests are synthetic. Source-root lineage is explicitly unqualified; no independent-source count is inferred. Broader context is not fabricated. Current time filters are valid/event time, not an as-known-then reconstruction.

Remaining before complete initial-release Markets: independent review; complete canonical alias/temporal ambiguity and method-admission qualification; verified source/root lineage and exact attribution obligations; production-authoritative rights/privacy binding for market materials; public publication decision bindings (existing generic assessments stay private and public validator remains unchanged); full exposed-reader inventory; real-data equity/crypto/indirect journeys; reusable asset card, dedicated workspace and supported two-way shared-surface navigation; explicit deployment authorization. Quotes, TradingView and CoinMarketCap remain separately gated. No new fee, credential, provider, production write or owner-device project file is authorized here.

Execution evidence and failures remain on the draft PR. A green mechanism test does not establish production rights, publication or complete Markets.

## Bounded discovery and deterministic identity inputs
The recursive input is capped at sixteen typed candidates whose exact capture, endpoint, edge and optional companion versions are retained by the requested workspace observation. The seventeenth fails closed before recursion; final response LIMIT is not the work bound. Adjacent hops must share the exact retained node version, not only node UUID. Candidate fan-out is covered by a separate retained observation; newly appended candidates cannot enter an older frozen observation. Saturation fails closed without returning a trimmed successful subset. This cap is a resource qualification limit, not support for arbitrary production corpus size; a separately qualified bounded frontier traversal is required before larger workloads. Request timestamps require explicit offsets and at most PostgreSQL microsecond precision; relative, date-only, timezone-less and finer timestamps are rejected before authentication/query.

Private path projections retain permission-checked node ID/version/type/name, issuer/network ID/version/type/name, asset validity/identifier and aliases tied to the asset version. The existing retained excerpt provides exact material hash/version, input position, field and span; it does not prove primary-source/root independence or complete rights/attribution metadata. Those absent provenance contracts remain BLOCKED. Empty paths do not provide a standalone qualified asset card, and no browser endpoint is implemented. This is a backend prerequisite, not completed MK-1 or a Markets workspace.

# Markets prerequisite contract qualification

Base: 267c36dec6c39afafbab4494efffc83d01a6a752 (PR #120).
This is server-side semantic contract preparation, not a deployed Markets endpoint,
public asset registry, new publisher or completed Markets release.

## Reconciled existing state

Read-only survivor inspection found zero public.entities rows, one public.nodes
row of type event, seven retained record versions (five article, one graph_node,
one temporal_assessment) and one supported private assessment. Node types are
event/actor/institution/document/anomaly/policy/topic; stock instruments and
cryptoassets are not yet canonical node types. Do not infer assets from ticker
text or silently treat a company, listing, network and token as the same identity.

Reuse evidence_pipeline.record_versions, exact article captures, candidate spans,
assessments, roots and dependency invalidations. Existing candidate spans use
PostgreSQL Unicode code-point offsets; the contract follows that convention.
The existing private assessment release_state is constrained to private and
read_assessment reports publicly_eligible=false. No contract flag can authorize
changing that state or making those rows available to anonymous readers.

## Qualified semantic boundary

marketsEvidenceContract.mjs is a pure server-side validator with no runtime caller.
It accepts a bounded proposed projection from a future trusted retained-record
adapter, never public request JSON as authority. It checks:

- Canonical UUID plus exact identity record version; equity issuer identity;
  crypto network plus asset identifier; namespace-qualified, half-open dated
  aliases. A symbol never becomes an identity.
- One to eight connected, acyclic, explicitly typed essential relationship hops;
  exact assessment IDs and candidate IDs, supported outcome, no stale/superseded
  decision, valid interval and explicit release eligibility.
- Every hop's exact capture/span/excerpt, article and shared root identity,
  retained payload hash, publication text, recorded timestamp and versioned
  excerpt rights/attribution. Permission loss or corrected bytes fails closed.
- Nanosecond-exact interval comparisons with explicit offsets; source publication
  text, including date-only precision, is retained without midnight invention.
- A narrow output projection that does not forward arbitrary private properties.
  No price fields, composite confidence, independent-source count or causal verdict.

The supplied at is valid/event time, not as-known-then time. Historical knowledge
must come from a retained observation; this validator does not reconstruct it.
Shared root IDs are preserved, not asserted to be independently verified.
Right/publication booleans are required adapter inputs, not security credentials
or standalone proof of publication, ownership, source authenticity or licensing.

## Release prerequisites still pending

A production integration must implement and qualify typed canonical asset history,
version/alias/source bindings, a trusted authorized reader and existing publication
decision references. Validate rights records and exact stored versions in the
database; never trust caller-supplied booleans. It must wire direct reporting,
connected developments and separately labelled broader context into shared views,
then prove stock and crypto journeys plus an indirect path on retained real data.
No parallel graph, new private-to-public shortcut or synthetic production assets.

The current snapshot has no eligible market identity/path. A new empty UI cannot
stand in for those prerequisites. No Markets tab, numerical quote feed, TradingView
embed or CoinMarketCap integration is enabled by this batch. Account-specific
rights and quota proof remain required; there are no new fees/providers.

The unit examples are explicitly synthetic and run only in CI. They establish
contract counterexamples, not real assets, relationships, reviews or publications.
All existing tests/builds and postmerge live checks remain required. Results are
recorded on the PR. Overall Markets and backend consolidation remain incomplete.

drop policy if exists citations_public_read on public.citations;
create policy citations_public_read
  on public.citations
  for select
  to anon, authenticated
  using (
    exists (
      select 1
      from public.articles a
      where a.id = citations.article_id
        and a.reader_state = 'eligible'
        and a.source_status = 'active'
    )
  );

drop policy if exists node_location_mentions_public_read on public.node_location_mentions;
drop policy if exists sky_verifications_public_read on public.sky_verifications;

revoke select on table public.node_location_mentions from anon, authenticated, public;
revoke select on table public.sky_verifications from anon, authenticated, public;
grant select on table public.node_location_mentions, public.sky_verifications to service_role;

create or replace view public.graph_coverage_public
with (security_barrier = true, security_invoker = false)
as
with article_totals as (
  select count(*)::integer as article_count
  from public.articles
  where reader_state = 'eligible'
    and source_status = 'active'
),
resolved_article_totals as (
  select count(distinct c.article_id)::integer as articles_with_published_node
  from public.citations c
  inner join public.articles a
    on a.id = c.article_id
   and a.reader_state = 'eligible'
   and a.source_status = 'active'
  where c.resolved_node_id is not null
),
pending_graph_candidates as (
  select count(*)::integer as pending_graph_candidate_count
  from public.cross_surface_candidates c
  where c.candidate_type in ('graph_node', 'graph_edge')
    and c.review_state in ('pending', 'owner_hold')
),
published_graph as (
  select
    (select count(*)::integer from public.nodes) as published_node_count,
    (select count(*)::integer from public.edges) as documented_relationship_count
)
select
  a.article_count,
  r.articles_with_published_node,
  greatest(a.article_count - r.articles_with_published_node, 0)::integer as articles_without_published_node,
  p.pending_graph_candidate_count,
  g.published_node_count,
  g.documented_relationship_count
from article_totals a
cross join resolved_article_totals r
cross join pending_graph_candidates p
cross join published_graph g;

revoke insert, update, delete, truncate on public.graph_coverage_public from public, anon, authenticated;
grant select on public.graph_coverage_public to anon, authenticated, service_role;

comment on view public.graph_coverage_public is
  'Anonymous aggregate coverage disclosure. Article and resolved-citation counts follow the eligible+active reader contract. Pending, withheld, and withdrawn records are excluded. Review-state candidate counts remain aggregates only.';
